dedupe_keys.name: colonial pipeline ransomware shutdown and federal response may 2021

description: On 7 May 2021 the Colonial Pipeline Company proactively shut down its pipeline system after a ransomware attack, and on 13 May it announced that the whole system had restarted and deliveries had resumed to all markets. The DOE CESER page records the federal response. DOE's Energy Response Organization was activated to coordinate with industry, other agencies and states, give situational awareness and impact analysis, and help move fuel to affected areas. The FBI confirmed on 10 May that DarkSide ransomware was responsible, and CISA and the FBI issued a joint advisory on 11 May. The Department of Transportation granted temporary hours-of-service exemptions for fuel carriers (9 May, later adding West Virginia), allowed overweight fuel loads on Interstates in states with recent disaster declarations, and coordinated its maritime, rail, highway and pipeline administrations; PHMSA issued an enforcement stay; EPA issued emergency fuel waivers for the District of Columbia and states from Pennsylvania to Louisiana; and FERC's chairman called for mandatory pipeline cyber standards. Coverage: the East Coast and Southeast fuel supply. Access: a public page linking agency statements. Licence and cost: free, US government work. Caveats: a chronology of official actions, not an impact analysis. It illustrates emergency response and cascading effects of a pipeline outage on road fuel logistics. It relates to the pipeline cyber-physical incident panel, CISA exploited vulnerabilities and PHMSA incident data in the catalogue.
